clue.text: Film-maker in favour of Frank replacing the lead

indicators.note: one word takes the place of the opening letter of another, so the first letter is swapped out

blocks.note: frank means candid and straightforward
to be for something is to be in favour of it

explanation.surface: A frank film-maker who backs a recasting of the leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR loses its lead letter F, and DIRECT takes its place, giving DIRECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is the person in charge of making a movie, guiding actors and crew.

clue.text: Resolve to cut 10%, subtract 50%, and add 50% of the remainder

indicators.note: taking away half means the second half of the word is dropped
adding something means joining it on at the end

blocks.note: to decimate originally meant to kill one in ten
the first half of what is left after the cut

explanation.surface: A finance plan: resolve to make a series of percentage cuts and additions.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of DECIMATE leaves DECI; half of DECI is DE, added on to give DECIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on something is to settle it in your mind, to make up your mind about it.

clue.text: What's required to release answer stored in memory?

indicators.note: something stored is kept inside, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer
ans. is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A computing question about what is needed to free a saved answer from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' suggests freeing up computer memory; it means freeing a hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the money demanded by kidnappers, which must be paid for a captive to be released.

clue.text: Penalise footballer over accidental cheat

blocks.note: a referee penalises a player by showing a yellow or red card
in music an accidental is a sign such as a sharp or flat

explanation.surface: A referee punishes a player for an accidental foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accidental' reads as unintended, but is the musical sign; 'over' just puts CARD above it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional cheat who wins at card games by trickery.

clue.text: Unconventional course has introduction moved nearer conclusion

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted toward the end, so the word's letters change order

blocks.note: a route is a course taken

explanation.surface: An unusual training course moves its opening session toward the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the start of ROUTE moves to just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a French loan word for bizarre or beyond the bounds of convention.

clue.text: This describes the return of Hamlet, perhaps, and his end

definitions.text: This describes the return of Hamlet, perhaps, and his end

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: his refers to Hamlet, so this is the last letter of that name
Hamlet is a well-known British brand of cigar

explanation.surface: A theatre note on Shakespeare's prince coming home to Denmark and then dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is both the prince and a British brand of small cigar; the end of Hamlet is T, and RAGIC is the cigar turned round, giving TRAGIC. The whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's homecoming and death form one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, so the word describing it is the adjective for such drama.

clue.text: Religious and physical education associated with dawn of New Age

indicators.note: dawn is the start of the day, so only the first letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject
PE is the usual abbreviation
first letter of New

explanation.surface: School subjects linked to the start of a New Age spiritual movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' reads as one phrase; 'Age' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to mature or grow older, which is what fruit or cheese does when it ripens.

clue.text: Almost understand about life in Ancient Rome's importance

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
about means around, so these letters go round the next word

blocks.note: to grasp is to understand
vita is the Latin word for life

explanation.surface: Nearly comprehending the significance of life in Ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASP loses its P, and GRAS wraps around the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is dignity and seriousness of manner, a weightiness that gives someone importance; it is also a Roman virtue.

clue.text: Talk about touching one of Nina's parts

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, about
on means touching, resting against
a verse is one section of a song, such as one by the singer Nina Simone

explanation.surface: A conversation about touching one part of a woman called Nina.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa is a standard abbreviation for about.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, to hold a conversation.

clue.text: Material that may be used by construction firm

definitions.text: Material that may be used by construction

blocks.clueFragment: Material that may be used by construction
blocks.note: first meaning: the building material of cement, sand and gravel
second meaning: solid, definite, as in firm evidence

explanation.walkthrough: 'construction firm' reads as one phrase, a building company, but it splits: the first part is one meaning and 'firm' is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a builder's mixture of cement and aggregate and, as an adjective, means solid or definite rather than vague.

clue.text: Twist right ankle initially during cycle ride

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
something happening during an event sits inside it, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: a spin is a short ride, for instance on a bicycle
R is the standard abbreviation for right
first letter of ankle

explanation.surface: A cyclist turns their right ankle while out on a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain a joint is to wrench or twist it so the ligaments are injured.

clue.text: Fair trade in the centre of Belize for two-thirds of capital

indicators.note: trading in the middle of a word means giving its central letters up in exchange for others

blocks.note: the Central American country, taken as written
the first four of the six letters of London, the UK capital

explanation.surface: Fair trade in Belize, swapping goods for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair trade' reads as one ethical phrase; Fair is the definition. The centre of BELIZE, ELIZ, is traded for LOND.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, and a person with such hair is called blonde.

clue.text: Refuse to put on clothes after losing heart for nothing

indicators.note: the middle letter is given up and something else is taken in exchange for it

blocks.note: to dress is to put clothes on
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declines to get dressed, having lost the will to bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: rubbish. DRESS swaps its central E for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, rubbish, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Rose for one soldier breaking rank

indicators.note: breaking into a line means pushing in between its parts, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
a rank is a row or line of soldiers
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier steps out of his rank to pick a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose for one' looks like the definition with its example marker, but 'for one' gives EG, and the soldier is an insect, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild species of the rose family with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Engineer sends man away for resources

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rebuild, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer is sent away to fetch supplies for a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun, a person, but works as a verb telling you to rebuild the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways and means are the methods and funds available for getting something done, so they are resources.

clue.text: Sub perhaps yearns to have some editing work

indicators.note: editing reworks and rearranges material, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sub-editor longs for some editing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a sub-editor; it is a sub roll. A sarney (or sarnie) is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub is a long submarine sandwich roll, one example of a sandwich, which is what sarney means in British slang.

clue.text: Presumably this has little need for Fat Controller on today's network?

definitions.text: Presumably this has little need for Fat Controller on today's network?

blocks.clueFragment: Presumably this has little need for Fat Controller on today's network?
blocks.note: surface reading: a modern railway has no use for the Fat Controller, the stout railway boss in the Thomas the Tank Engine stories
setter's reading: a tiny component, so not a fat one, that controls devices on computer networks today

explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Controller is the railway manager in the Thomas the Tank Engine children's books; the clue turns 'little' and 'Fat' into the size of a computing part and 'network' into a computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny silicon integrated circuit acts as the controlling brain in modern networked electronic devices.

clue.text: Attach warning under a protective cover

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under something means coming after it

blocks.note: to pin is to fasten or attach
taken as written
fore is the golfer's shouted warning

explanation.surface: Fix a warning sign beneath a protective sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or overall worn to protect clothes beneath it.

clue.text: God interrupting farewell upset balloonist

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up
to interrupt is to break in, so this goes inside the other word

blocks.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A divine visitor interrupts an upsetting goodbye for a balloon pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye; in a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so it reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerostat is a lighter-than-air craft such as a balloon, and the word is also used for a balloon pilot.

clue.text: Go through to the rear of trendy "green" property

indicators.note: being at the back of something means coming after it, so this word follows the other

blocks.note: in means fashionable
to experience something is to go through it

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly building has a fashionable feature you walk through to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green property' suggests an environmentally friendly house; here green means callow, and the property is the quality of being so.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means being new and untried, so the quality or attribute of greenness is a lack of practical knowledge.

clue.text: Children's author briefly taking to poet

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A children's writer briefly takes up poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: MILNE loses its final E, and MILN holds TO.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the seventeenth-century English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Relief of snooker player completing short break

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the last letter goes
completing something means coming at its end, so this goes after

blocks.note: a rest is a break
a cue is what plays the ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player gets relief by finishing off a short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a snooker break, a run of pots, but it is a pause. The snooker player is the cue, the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue brings relief, deliverance from danger, as in the relief of a besieged town.

clue.text: Agreed auditor's intended payment to correct errors

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: at one means in agreement
meant means intended

explanation.surface: An accountant's approved bill to put right some bookkeeping mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant checking errors, but it is just a hearer: MEANT said out loud gives MENT. AT ONE is the phrase for being in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is reparation for wrongdoing, making amends, which is a kind of paying for one's mistakes.

clue.text: Cycling match is a bore

indicators.note: letters going round as on a wheel, so some move from front to back while keeping their order

blocks.note: to match is to agree, correspond

explanation.surface: Someone calls a cycle race a tedious event.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of AGREE moves round to the front, the other letters keeping their order. 'Cycling' looks like the sport, and 'bore' like dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river estuary such as the Trent.

clue.text: No good will come from doing casual work for these rates

indicators.note: coming from somewhere means leaving it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: NG is the abbreviation for no good
temping is working as a temporary employee

explanation.surface: A temp doing casual work won't do well at these rates of pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' suggests pay rates, but these are musical speeds; tempi is the Italian plural of tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi are the speeds at which pieces of music are played, rates of performance.

clue.text: Sheepish lover removes jacket and trousers at home

indicators.note: taking off a jacket strips the outside layer, so the first and last letters go
as a verb, to trouser is to pocket something, so these letters are taken inside

blocks.note: taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An embarrassed lover undresses at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassment, but it is the literal sense: like a sheep. 'trousers' is a verb, to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to or resembling sheep, which is the literal sense of sheepish.

clue.text: One's left powerless after this heartless atrocity

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

blocks.note: an outrage is a shocking, cruel act

explanation.surface: A victim of a cruel atrocity is left helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' suggests helplessness after a crime, but it is literal: with no electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a cut in the electricity supply, after which a household has no power.

clue.text: "Stressful" impact he might make

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the anxious effect a man might have.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag that 'Stressful' is not its usual meaning of anxiety-causing but full of stress, as in emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic speech puts strong weight or force on its words, so it is literally full of stress.

clue.text: Value opponents holding hands by side we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word before is spelt as another word that sounds the same

blocks.note: in bridge, East and South sit as opponents, each holding a hand of cards
a team is a side in sport

explanation.surface: Rivals clasp hands next to a team they admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding hands' looks affectionate, but it is cards: bridge players are named by compass points and E and S are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to rate them highly, to value or respect them.

clue.text: Hand out pass admitting writer on board ship

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so the following letters go inside
a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: to pass away is to die
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A boarding pass is issued to a writer joining a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a noun, a boarding pass, but it is the verb meaning to die. SS is the usual crossword ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or give out, which is what handing out means.
